findings.problem: ShardWorkflow struct allows invariant-violating states: status can be 'sent' while is_sent is false, or status can be 'pending' while is_sent is true. sent_at_epoch_ms can be None while is_sent is true. is_validated is a bare bool with no enforcement that validated shards are frozen.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mutate shard fields into contradictory states (e.g. is_sent=true with status='pending'), breaking downstream logic that assumes sent shards have status='sent' and a non-null sent_at_epoch_ms. This enables silent data corruption in the shard workflow pipeline.
findings.fix: Replace status/is_sent/is_validated with a single typed enum or typestate. Use newtype or enum for status (e.g. enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }) so sent-at and status are coupled in the same variant. Remove pub fields; use constructors that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: All fields of ShardWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate any field without invariant checks. This directly enables creating invalid states that the struct cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can set item.is_sent = false while item.status = "sent", or set is_validated = true and then modify the shard. No constructor or accessor enforces domain invariants.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a sealed constructor or builder that enforces invariants. Replace with an enum or typestate so valid states are the only constructable ones.

findings.problem: status is a String, allowing any arbitrary string value (e.g. 'SENT', 'sent!', '') instead of a well-defined set of states. mark_sent on line 10 writes a magic string literal 'sent' which is error-prone.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, case mismatches, or injection into status break state-matching logic. The magic string 'sent' on line 10 is not compile-time checked against any enum variant.
findings.fix: Replace String status with an enum: enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }. mark_sent returns the Sent variant with the epoch_ms baked in.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are bare bools that don't capture the directional lifecycle. A shard can be both is_validated=true and is_sent=true, or neither, with no enforcement of valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: No compile-time or runtime enforcement of valid state transitions (pending -> validated -> sent). Bool flags are independent and can be set in any order or combination, enabling states like validated-but-unsent or unsent-but-marked-sent.
findings.fix: Replace bool flags with a typestate enum or a single enum capturing the full lifecycle: enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }. Transition functions return the next enum variant.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> independent of is_sent. A shard can be is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123).
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code expecting sent_at_epoch_ms to be populated for sent shards will encounter None, causing panics on unwrap() or incorrect behavior on Some/None branches.
findings.fix: Bake sent_at into the Sent variant of the status enum: enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }. Remove is_sent and sent_at_epoch_ms as separate fields.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status='sent' and is_sent=true but does NOT set sent_at_epoch_ms. The field remains None or its previous value, violating the invariant that sent shards record their send time.
findings.failure_mode: Sent shards lack temporal metadata, breaking audit trails, retry deadlines, and SLA tracking that depend on sent_at_epoch_ms being set at send time.
findings.fix: mark_sent must accept epoch_ms as a parameter (or derive it from a clock abstraction) and store it in the Sent variant. Signature: pub fn mark_sent(item: ShardWorkflow, sent_at: u64) -> ShardStatus::Sent.

findings.problem: The domain model uses primitive types (String, bool) instead of domain newtypes/enums. This pushes all validation into imperative shell code rather than making illegal states unrepresentable at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Every caller must independently validate shard invariants. No compiler enforcement means bugs accumulate in shell code rather than being caught at compile time.
findings.fix: Define domain types: enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }. ShardWorkflow owns only the status type and id. All transitions go through pure functions that return the new status.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() performs an unnecessary heap allocation. With an enum status, no allocation is needed for state transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every mark_sent call. While not a correctness bug, it violates the performance discipline of avoiding allocations in pure pipelines.
findings.fix: Replace with enum assignment: item.status = ShardStatus::Sent { sent_at }. No heap allocation needed.
